To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the expression of PTHrp, TNF-alpha IL-6 and -11 is higher in the group of patients with invasion of the mandible by lower gingival squamos cell carcinoma than in the group without such invasion.
PTHrP and TNF-alpha, as well as IL-6 and 11, play an essential role in the mechanism by which bone is invaded by lower gingival squamocellular carcinoma.

the invasion group showed a higher level of expression of osteoclast-derived cytokines, PTHrP and TNF-alpha, and cancer-derived cytokines IL-6 and II-11, than the non-invasion group, whereas there was no significant difference in the levels between these two groups with respect to the expression of IL-18 and TGF-b.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism of mandibular bone invasion by gingival squamous carcinoma.
the role of cytokines in mandible invasion by gingival cancer.
the mechanism of bone destruction by carcinoma of the lower gingiva and provides evidence of the role of osteoclast-derived cytokines in bone destruction by squamous cell carcinomas
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the expression of PTH-rP, TNF-α and IL-6 are associated with bone invasion of lower gingival squamocellular carcinoma.
osteoclast-related factors are associated with bone invasion in lower gingival squamocellular carcinoma.
the mechanism of bone metastasis is not fully understood and that the role of PTHrPs in this process is not fully elucidated.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the cytokines PTHrP and TNF-alpha, and the interleukins IL-1, -6, and -11, play a role in bone invasion by mandibular squamous cell carcinoma.
the expression of PTHrp, TNF-alpha and IL-6 in the invasion group is significantly greater than that in the non-invasion group.

cytokines are involved in the process of bone invasion and the cytokines may be used as prognostic factors in the management of mandibular invasion.

The main takeaway from our work is that

the presence of PTHrPs in tumor cells and the expression of TNF-alpha, interleukin-6, and interleukin-11 in tumor cells and infiltrating mononuclear cells may be associated with bone invasion by lower gingival squa-mous cell carcinomas.
the expression of PTHrp, IL-6, IL-11 and TNF-α in the cancer tissue is related to the occurrence of bone invasion.
the expression of osteoclast related cytokines in mandible invasion by squamous carcinoma is associated with the presence of bone invasion.
